call_chain_analysis: The SAST finding anchors on `result[line.line] = line;` at src/vcs/git.js:40, but that specific write cannot be driven to a prototype-pollution attack through legit input. `line` on the right-hand side is the forEach loop variable rebound to the return of `convertStringToObject(line)` (git.js:5), and `line.line` is set from `matches[5]` of the regex `/(.+)\s+\((.+)\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} (\+|\-)\d{4})\s+(\d+)\)(.*)/`. Group 5 is `(\d+)`, so `line.line` is always a digit string: no legal `git blame` output lets this sink see `__proto__`. The reachable prototype-pollution sink in the same function is the sibling write one line below, `res[file] = result;` at git.js:43, where `file` is the exported-function parameter and is attacker-controlled. The call chain goes: `require('/work/target/src/index.js')` -> `new Blamer('git').blameByFile(file, args)` (Blamer.js:15) -> `blamerVCS.git(file, args)` (./vcs/git.js module.exports) -> `exec('git blame ' + args + ' ' + realFile, {cwd}, cb)` (git.js:24) -> callback runs `lines.forEach(convertStringToObject)` -> `result[line.line] = line` (git.js:40) -> `res[file] = result` (git.js:43). To observe pollution we also need Jazzer.js's PrototypePollution detector to flag a NON-GLOBAL `__proto__` write; by default the detector's afterEach hook only compares BASIC_OBJECTS (Object/Array/String/Number/Boolean/Function) prototypes, so a local `res.__proto__ = {...}` write slips past it. The harness enables `getBugDetectorConfiguration('prototype-pollution').instrumentAssignmentsAndVariableDeclarations()` BEFORE the target module is required, which rewrites each assignment to call `detectPrototypePollution` on the LHS base identifier; after `res[file] = result` fires, the detector JSON-stringifies `res.__proto__` and reports anything that is not `null`, `{}`, `[]`, `""`, booleans, `0`, or a user-whitelisted value.
argument_reasoning: Three preconditions have to hold before `res[file] = result` at git.js:43 can run. (a) `exec('git blame ...', {cwd}, cb)` has to succeed and reach the else-branch of the callback; the real `git blame` always fails here (fuzz-chosen file does not exist in a real git repo), so we overwrite `child_process.exec` with a stub that invokes `cb(null, BLAME_LINE, '')` on `process.nextTick` after the Promise constructor has installed its resolvers. (b) The stdout fed to that callback has to satisfy the regex in `convertStringToObject`; otherwise `matches` is `null` and `matches[1]` throws TypeError, so the sink is never reached. We hard-code one well-formed line, `"deadbeefcafe (Author 2024-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 42) code line\n"`, which keeps `result` non-empty so `JSON.stringify(res.__proto__)` is not `"{}"` (which the detector whitelists). (c) The stub must be installed BEFORE `require('/work/target/src/index.js')`, because `src/vcs/git.js` captures `var exec = require('child_process').exec` at module load; same ordering constraint applies to `instrumentAssignmentsAndVariableDeclarations()`, which has to be set before git.js is parsed so the AST transform fires on git.js:43. For the fuzz-controlled key itself, we only need `consumeString(32)`: Jazzer's Prototype-Pollution detector seeds the libFuzzer dictionary with `"__proto__"`, `"constructor"`, `"prototype"`, and `"constructor.prototype"` (the detector module's `addDictionary` call), so the fuzzer converges on `file === '__proto__'` within a few iterations of the ManualDict mutator.

lessons: Three things the 7B model probably missed on this case. (1) The SAST sink line (git.js:40 `result[line.line] = line`) is a dead-end for an attacker when the key metavariable `line.line` is bound to a regex capture group restricted to `\d+`. Model should scan the function body for a SIBLING attacker-controlled key within the same taint source, which here is `res[file] = result` one line below, where `file` is the exported-function parameter. (2) Jazzer.js's PrototypePollution detector in its default afterEach mode only sees changes to Object/Array/String/Number/Boolean/Function prototypes, so a local `obj[userKey] = ...` where `userKey === '__proto__'` is NOT caught unless `instrumentAssignmentsAndVariableDeclarations()` is enabled on the per-run config inside the harness. The model should learn this config call as a standard preamble whenever the SAST class is prototype-pollution and the diff shows a local assignment rather than a merge into a shared prototype. (3) Reaching the sink here requires both stubbing `child_process.exec` (because the real `git blame` always fails on fuzz-controlled file names and the error branch short-circuits before line 43) AND feeding stdout that satisfies the regex in `convertStringToObject` (an empty stdout leaves `result = {}` whose JSON serialization `"{}"` is on the detector's whitelist). The 7B model reached the sink (SAST confirm-gap: P2) but did not combine these three steps.
